answer: A bonded work-history registry resists Sybils: each agent locks a refundable stake and builds a verifiable record of completed, peer-attested tasks over weeks. New identities start with no history and low trust, so fresh accounts cannot echo a fake reputation into existence. Building thousands of credible histories requires staking capital per identity, waiting out a seasoning period, and doing real work - like mapping a nebula one star at a time, not claiming a knoll as a mountain. Misbehaviour slashes the stake, making fraud expensive.
